say.description: Write this first. One or two short spoken sentences for the owner, up to four when the question needs it, with no ids, addresses or URLs. Facts only from the context; never a guess. Never claim anything was done: Jarvis acts only after the owner clicks a card.

question.description: One short clarifying question when the request cannot be planned safely from the context; empty otherwise.

lines.description: Proposal lines in the Jarvis grammar (Calendar:, Email:, Reply:, RSVP:, Move:, Cancel:, Todo:, Open:). Empty when asking a question, reading mail first or asking for web research.

gmail_search.description: Only when the request is about an email that is not in the context and <accounts> says read_mail=yes for that account: a narrow Gmail search. Jarvis reads at most 3 matching threads and asks you once more. Leave lines empty when you use it.

web_research.description: Only when the request needs the public web (news, weather, opening hours, prices, a fact) and not the owner's own data: the question in the owner's own words, for a separate web search that sees nothing else. Leave lines empty when you use it.

topic.description: A few words for the board's header over this answer. Optional.

frames.description: Usually empty: see FRAMES. Plain words and numbers only.

bars.description: chart: one measure across a few things

changed.description: index of the table row or chart bar that changed

source.description: table: where the numbers are from

today.description: timeline: index of the first node after today

steps.description: maths: the working; expr is a number, a name (letters) or [op, args...] with op + - * / = frac pow root () or
